about.title: Taft Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Taft's economy runs on oil, agriculture, and the small businesses that support both, which means work injuries here often involve heavy equipment, vehicles, or contractors moving between job sites along corridors like 6th Street and Kern Street. When a worker gets hurt, California's workers' compensation system is usually the first stop, covering medical care and partial wage loss no matter who was at fault. But that system doesn't always cover everything, and it doesn't apply to everyone involved in an accident. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to the injury, a separate claim against that third party may be possible alongside a workers' comp case. We are an independent team that handles work injury cases and can look at the full picture, including whether a third-party claim applies. We will explain your options clearly.
commonInjuries: Back and spinal strain from lifting or falls
Crush injuries from heavy machinery or oilfield equipment
Traumatic brain injury from falls at height
Burns from equipment or chemical exposure
Injuries from vehicle collisions during work travel

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Taft Work Injury

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Whole Story
items.desc: California treats workers' comp as the usual exclusive remedy against an employer, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker can still be held separately liable. We can help sort out whether a third-party claim applies to your situation.

items.title: Deadlines Work Differently for Each Claim
items.desc: Reporting a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days is required to preserve your workers' comp rights, while a separate third-party claim generally carries a two-year deadline. Missing either window can limit your options.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from punishing workers for reporting an injury or filing a claim. We can help you understand your rights if you feel pressured after speaking up.

items.question: I was hurt on an oilfield job near Taft — do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: In most cases, workers' compensation is the first path against your employer regardless of fault. But if equipment failure, a subcontractor, or another company's negligence contributed to the accident, a separate third-party claim may also be possible. We can review the details and explain which paths apply to you.

items.question: What if my injury happened during a shift change near Gardner Field Road or 6th Street?
items.answer: Injuries that happen while traveling for work duties, rather than a normal commute, can sometimes involve both workers' comp and a separate claim if another driver was negligent. Weekend evening hours, like Saturdays around 7 to 9 p.m. when reported crashes tend to cluster locally, are worth mentioning to us. The specific circumstances matter, so we look closely at the timeline.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for reporting a workplace injury in Taft?
items.answer: No. California law makes it illegal for an employer to retaliate against a worker for reporting an injury or pursuing a workers' comp claim. If you believe you've faced retaliation, we can help you understand what protections may apply.
